title: Writing to a text file
code:
f = open("test.txt","w")
f.write("This is the first Line")
f.write("This is the second line")
f.close()

f = open("test.txt","a")
f.write("Yet another line")
f.close()

lines.explanation: opens file with name of "test.txt" Here we give 2 arguments. The first as we know specifies the name of the text file. The second argument specifies the mode of writing. 'w' stands for write. When we open the text file using the mode 'w' it erases the existing data and writes the new data that we specify
This statement writes the following string into the text file
Writing another line into the text file
Once we have written all the required lines into the text file, we close the connection to the text file

opens file with name of "test.txt". Here the second argument we specified is 'a' which stands for append. This means that it does not delete the existing data when the new data is written but it appends the new data at the end of the file
Finally when we are done appending the new data, we close the connection to the file
